findings.sourceReading: 指し間違えた手 is a move already played incorrectly; 待て here requests a takeback, which Nanjo refuses. The comparison concerns each friend refusing the other a concession.
findings.alternative: 待て can ordinarily mean wait, and Japanese does not state every subject. But the already-made mistaken move and chess setting support the takeback reading; they do not support the invented warning about a future move.

findings.description: Battler denies having the romantic exploits Eva imagines and says he would rather have her introduce him to someone (紹介してほしい). WH replaces that request with “I’d rather it did,” whose antecedent is the supposedly weird experience of leaving girls crying. The reply changes from an inexperienced young man asking for help meeting girls into wishing the alleged exploits had happened.
